49.original: We have no reason to doubt Vrtra. Let us depart for Garlemald as soon as possible.

50.original: So that was a dragon's roar. Quite a trick, imbuing one's voice with aether.

51.original: By all accounts, Azdaja is Golbez's prisoner, yet if she was in the Source...

52.original: It could be that she managed to escape from the void, if only for a fleeting moment.

53.original: But that is mere conjecture. If we want the truth, then we must go and find it.

55.original: Come, let's make for Tertium. Our friends are waiting.

56.original: I thought to depart from Radz-at-Han sooner, but Y'shtola insisted I bring warmer clothes.

57.original: This vessel does not feel cold as such, but she reminded me that, so long as I am Varshahn, it would be prudent not to appear overly conspicuous.

58.original: I trust you know the “associates” who will be joining us. Hopefully they have been keeping well.

59.original: People live in such places, do they? Not that I would presume to know their preferences, but it seems...uncomfortable.

60.original: I had tempered my hopes, but thanks to Alphinaud and Alisaie, we might yet learn something of Azdaja.

61.original: Nothing appears to be out of the ordinary here at the camp. Let us see what we find at this village.

62.original: I knew the twins wouldn't disappoint.

63.original: A village of voidsent users... Lest you think I have feelings on this─I don't. What others do is not my concern.

64.original: I expect it's been a while since you spoke with Jullus. He will be glad to see you.

65.original: The people here struggle to survive as it is. The last thing they need is for Garlemald to be overrun with voidsent.

67.original: And I see you're traveling with a large crew as usual...

68.original: Not to suggest that's an inconvenience for us. We'd be happy to share our supplies with you and your allies, should you require any.

70.original: Apologies if we interrupt, Jullus, but there is a matter we wish to discuss.

71.original: We've just finished our routine briefing, so you come at a good time. Is this about the voidsent?

72.original: It is. From what we can discern, they're coming from the mountains to the east.

73.original: Practitioners of the reaper arts once lived in that area, did they not?

74.original: Yes, they had a village there in the Lapis Manalis caverns.

75.original: The scythe-wielders forged pacts with voidsent, and took to battle with the beings at their side. For a time they played an invaluable role in our military, but the advent of magitek saw them fall out of favor.

76.original: And when some were unmasked as insurrectionists, the order was outlawed. The village is believed to be long abandoned.

77.original: Speaking of their art...it seems you've picked it up. Who was it that taught you?

78.original: ...Well, I suppose it's neither here nor there now.

79.original: My sister has been taken captive by voidsent. I sensed her presence in this land, and have come in search of her.

80.original: If voidsent have been sighted here, then I believe there is a connection. We should like to investigate these caverns you mention, but Alphinaud tells us they are not easily reached.

81.original: I'm afraid so. Deep snow and tumultuous winds rule out walking and flying.

82.original: If you want to get anywhere, you're going to need a magitek snowcraft. Alas, the last remaining functional one we had has broken down. Should still be over in Cerulea Ingens, where it was abandoned.

83.original: Is there anyone who can fix it?

84.original: Perhaps the former engineers at Tapper's Den.

85.original: Their duty included transporting ceruleum tanks to Juturna Platform G using snowcraft. I expect they had to maintain a few over the years.

86.original: That's worth looking into, I'd say.

87.original: In the course of delivering provisions, I've come to know the people there quite well. If they can help us, I'm sure they will.

88.original: May I ask you to accompany her? Given the presence of voidsent, it's best that we avoid traveling alone.

89.original: In the meantime, will you not tell me more about the mountain? I would like to learn as much as I can before commencing our search in earnest.

90.original: Come with me. I'll introduce you to someone who's well versed in the local geography.

91.original: Alisaie, was it? I wish to speak with you.

92.original: In that case, why don't you come with us to Tapper's Den? We can chat on the way.

93.original: I shall go and brief the contingent on the voidsent issue, that they too may be prepared.

94.original: If you want to eavesdrop, be my guest. It doesn't matter to me.

96.original: We should get back to it, but before we do...

97.original: Are you all right, Zero? Did I say something that confused or upset you?

98.original: ...No. I'm simply trying to understand your perspective. If you wish to continue, I am ready and able.

99.original: Well, that's a relief! This isn't the sort of place you want to mull over things.

100.original: It's not much farther to Tapper's Den. I doubt we'll have much trouble finding an engineer when we arrive, so let's speak with the first one we spot.

101.original: This is one of the engineers, I think.

102.original: Because it's the right thing to do...

103.original: Wait, I know you. You're the one who roughed up the guards!

104.original: After you left, your contingent friends came along. Our lives are a lot easier now thanks to them.

105.original: They understood our plight, and offered to help─whether we wanted to stay here or return home. For that, we're truly grateful.

106.original: We're grateful to you too, Alisaie. The trip across the lake is hardly pleasant, but you make it all the same to bring us provisions.

107.original: Oh, don't mention it. We're just glad we can help.

108.original: That said, we were actually hoping to ask a favor of <hex:021A020203>you<hex:021A020103> today...

109.original: We need a magitek snowcraft repaired─the one abandoned in Cerulea Ingens. We were told you might be up to the task.

110.original: Ah, so you want to ride the mammoth!

111.original: That's what we took to calling the crafts on account of their size.

112.original: As often as I used them on rigs, I know a thing or two about their maintenance. I'll see if I can get your mammoth roaring again─it's the least I can do to repay your kindness.

113.original: Wonderful! Please come with us back to Camp Broken Glass, and we'll take it from there.

114.original: So far so good, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>! Let's be on our way.

115.original: Thank goodness we were able to find someone to help with repairs.

116.original: You mortals are more sensitive to the cold than I realized. My body is made differently, so I feel nothing.

117.original: Don't you worry─the mammoth is in good hands!

119.original: I presume this is the engineer who will help us with the craft?

120.original: I'll do everything I can to get her up and running again!

121.original: But I doubt I'll be able to do so quickly─at least on my own. The mammoth is big, and so are its parts. Some strong backs should make the work go faster.

123.original: You've finished learning about the mountain, I take it?

124.original: Aye, we have a solid grasp of that area, as well as the site of the snowcraft.

126.original: My back is perhaps not as strong as some, but I should be glad to stand guard for voidsent and other unruly wildlife.

127.original: Much obliged, miss. Then let's all head over to the mammoth and assess what needs fixing.

128.original: They have matters here well in hand. Which means we can resume our duties.

129.original: Would you care to assist us, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>?

131.original: I will assist you as well. As payment for answering my question.

132.original: It's hardly something that demands payment...but we'd be glad for your contribution nonetheless.
